templates.name: Hazard setup

templates.name: Logistic model: binary outcome
templates.description: Binary outcome logistic model, saving the fitted model, predictions and pooled inference across imputations.
templates.note: Measured by the 2026-09-21 content census: 3,393 SAS programs in 1,172 studies, including 1,781 multiply-imputed programs. The family-wide scan found 12,065 SAS programs in 1,220 study roots and 1,222 roots across all extensions; 25 SAS programs remain syntax-ambiguous and 15 are semantically misfiled. Prefix-wide breadth is recorded here in prose rather than copied into any qualifier's sas_breadth field.

templates.name: Random forest classifier: fit
templates.description: Grows a classification forest and checks it: out-of-bag error and the ROC curve with its AUC.

templates.note: Reads rfc.rds from rfc-fit in the same set and never refits. Census counts are on the fit row.

templates.description: Grows a random survival forest and checks it learned something: out-of-bag error, predicted survival and the Brier score.

templates.name: Random forest survival: explain
templates.description: Explains a saved survival forest: variable importance, VarPro and dependence plots. It never grows a forest.
templates.note: Reads rfs.rds from rfs-fit in the same set and never refits. Census counts are on the fit row.

templates.name: Single imputation
templates.note: Mean imputation is a step inside other jobs, bootstrap jobs chief among them, rather than a job type of its own: by job name 1 study carries an si program (2026-09-11 scan), and that is this row's sas_breadth_jobs. 223 studies call %imputsub, the single-mean-imputation macro, which runs PROC STANDARD ... REPLACE (measured 2026-09-05); that is a call-site count and stays in this note. Ported as hvtiRimputation::impute_mean(), shipped v0.1.0.

templates.name: Multiple imputation
templates.note: Multiple-imputation jobs are filed under bd, as bd jobs whose second name field names it (bd.mult_imput and its spellings, 17 studies), which is one job under two names (rule 2 of the catalog design, section 5). So sas_breadth_jobs counts the studies with either an mi program or such a bd job: 18, from the 2026-09-11 scan. 326 studies call %mult_imput, and 18 call both it and si's %imputsub (measured 2026-09-05); those are call-site counts and stay in this note. impute_multiple() is designed and not yet built; pooling by Rubin's rules is deferred.

templates.name: Random forest regression: fit
templates.description: Grows a regression forest and checks it: out-of-bag error and predicted against observed.
templates.note: Grows the regression forest and saves rfr.rds for rfr-explain in the same set. Old rfsrc.* and rf.* jobs map here by the outcome in their fit call. Gate measured 2026-09-19 by reading fit calls: six studies grow a regression forest.

templates.name: Random forest regression: explain
templates.description: Explains a saved regression forest: variable importance, VarPro and dependence plots.
templates.note: Reads rfr.rds from rfr-fit in the same set and never refits. Census counts are on the fit row.

templates.name: Descriptive: general
templates.description: First look at a built cohort: what the data contain, how each categorical variable breaks down, how each continuous variable is distributed, and which variables move together.
templates.note: Measured 2026-09-02: distinct studies with a program-extension job of this qualifier. Base procs only (contents/means/freq), no package dependency, which is what separates it from `tables`.

templates.name: Descriptive: formatted tables
templates.description: The formatted descriptive table: every reported variable under its section heading, categorical as n (%) and continuous as the summary you choose, written to Word.
templates.note: Measured 2026-09-02: distinct studies with a program-extension job of this qualifier. Calls %desc_tab, allocated to hvtiRtables. Same dataset and %vars as `general`; different destination package. PAIRWISE CORRELATION IS IN SCOPE for this row: the exemplar is /descriptive/dc.tables.ods_preoplabs_a1c.sas, a single `proc corr nosimple spearman pearson fisher(biasadj=no) plots=matrix` emitting a scatter-plot matrix and a Fisher-CI coefficient table, so it needs hv_correlation_matrix() in hvtiPlotR and hv_correlation_table() in hvtiRtables. `general` carries a plain `proc corr nosimple rank` section with no plot and no CIs; the two are not the same job.

templates.note: Measured 2026-09-02: distinct studies with a program-extension job of this qualifier.

templates.name: Descriptive: standardized differences
templates.note: Measured 2026-09-02: distinct studies with a program-extension job of this qualifier. Ships the 2019 successor (stddiff.sas, 649 lines, Artis, continuous+ordinal+categorical, hvtiRutilities), NOT the 2009 std_dif.sas (108 lines, hvtiRtables, 72 studies). Decided 2026-09-03; the wider corpus use of std_dif is a macro outliving its replacement, not a preference. Triage 2026-09-10: the legacy variants std_dif, stddif_mtch_mtwt, stdcoef_diff.continuous and stddiffci.sumtbl fold into this row rather than becoming qualifiers. Re-counted 2026-09-11 over the union of the spellings that fold here, by second name field in descriptive/dc: stddiff 59, std_dif 72, std_dif_all_bef-aft 13, stddiffci 8, stdcoef_diff 4, stddif_mtch_mtwt 1. That is 120 distinct studies, where adding them gives 157. The row keeps the 2019 spelling and counts every study using any of them (rule 2 of the catalog design, section 5). std_dif_all_bef-aft was folded in by the maintainer on 2026-09-11, beyond the triage's four. Owner moved 2026-09-16 from hvtiRutilities to hvtiRpropensity, whose ps_match, ps_logistic and ps_weight already compute standardized differences internally; the 2019 macro choice stands, and stddiffci (permutation reference) and mw_var (matching-weight variance) are ported with it. hvtiRutilities#103 is superseded by hvtiRpropensity#34. A census the same day found no study computing a matching weight across three or more groups: they compare groups two at a time, so the port is two-group only.

templates.name: Distribution of a variable
templates.note: ONE template, the variable as an EDIT: field. Measured 2026-09-03 over 1,271 distributions/dp job rows: 666 (52%) carry only the variable and no second field at all, and a measurement-scale word appears in 110 stems (8.7%) -- binary 51, ordinal 49, continuous 6. As a second qualifier, `binary` (8 studies) and `ordinal` (10) rank fifth and sixth behind `trend` (21), `tavr`, `gastroparesis` and `matched`. `qualifier` is `variable` rather than null because a prefix must be wholly qualified or wholly unqualified and graphs/dp is decomposed; it names what the job is parameterised by. Watch `trend` (100 rows, 21 studies), the one qualifier2 that could earn a template of its own.

templates.name: Descriptive plot: postage stamp
templates.description: Data-checking sweep over a new build: one small panel per variable against operation year, to find coding errors, drift and missingness. Not a manuscript figure.
templates.note: One small panel per VARIABLE across the whole dataset, parameterised by dataset rather than by variable, which is what separates it from `variable`. Exemplar is the legacy template tp.dp.DescriptiveSummary.qmd, already a Quarto file with an EDIT-here block and `# postage stamp plot grid size / ncol=4 / nrow=4`. Counts are null because descriptive/dp has never been censused; the 2026-09-02 decomposition enacted rows for graphs/dp and distributions/dp only. THIRD FOLDER for this prefix, and the first row whose folder disagrees with hvti_taxonomy() by design (dp maps to graphs there); see hvtiRtemplates#97, closed by hvtiRtemplates#98 on 2026-09-10, when blocked_on was cleared. Nothing checks blocked_on for a queued row, so a blocker naming a closed issue would have stood indefinitely and taught readers to distrust the column. The row was scaffold when hvtiPlotR 2.7.13 had no faceting constructor; the grid was the template's own facet_wrap(). Five further descriptive/dp legacy templates remain unrepresented. Still uncounted after the 2026-09-11 scan, on purpose: the job is named by dataset, not by a `postage` field. No descriptive/dp program carries `postage` as its second name field, and the word appears only inside seven graphs stems at one or two studies each, none of them this job. A literal-name count would read 0 and be wrong, so the count fields stay null. Engine decided 2026-09-14: hv_eda() earns the row (option 1 of the Lauren-lane decision), so her EDA report is the prototype this template is thin over.

templates.name: Descriptive plot: EDA report
templates.description: The whole data-checking report in one render: every column's contents, goodness of follow-up, then continuous variables and categorical variables as percentages and counts, each section with its table.
templates.note: A composite, not a new shape: its sections are dp-gfup, dc-gfup's tables and dp-postage, drawn through the same package functions (hv_followup_panels(), followup_check(), hv_eda_pages()) with the same arguments, so each section is the standalone job's figure. test-dp-eda.R checks that byte for byte against dp-postage. Asked for in the 2026-09-24 template review. Counts are null for the reason dp-postage's are: the legacy EDA report is named by dataset, not by an `eda` field.

options.name: Landmark early / late split
options.evidence: early / late: lg.dead 10 / 8, gm.mr 6 / 6, lm.af_po 6 / 4, dc.dead 4 / 5, lm.mr 4 / 4, dc.mr 3 / 3

One shared option, not a qualifier per prefix. See hvtiRtemplates dev/specs/2026-09-02-per-folder-naming-parse-design.md, section 8. Counts are distinct studies over the 2026-08-27 census, from job names; decided in the 2026-09-10 triage.
